claim: Measuring uncertainty in natural language generation directly from token/sequence probabilities is unreliable because of 'semantic equivalence' -- different sentences can express the same meaning, so semantic entropy is introduced as an entropy computed over meaning-clusters rather than raw sequences.
stance_target: naive token-probability entropy is a sufficient confidence measure for free-form generation
scope_conditions: general natural language generation, QA tasks tested
quoted_support: We show that measuring uncertainty in natural language is challenging because of "semantic equivalence" -- different sentences can mean the same thing. To overcome these challenges we introduce semantic entropy -- an entropy which incorporates linguistic invariances created by shared meanings.

claim: Semantic entropy is unsupervised, uses only a single model with no auxiliary classifier, and requires no modification to off-the-shelf language models.
stance_target: semantic entropy is architecturally simple to deploy relative to trained probes
quoted_support: Our method is unsupervised, uses only a single model, and requires no modifications to off-the-shelf language models.

claim: Comprehensive ablation studies show semantic entropy is more predictive of model accuracy on question-answering datasets than comparable baselines.
stance_target: semantic clustering over samples is a stronger accuracy predictor than baseline confidence measures
scope_conditions: QA datasets tested in the ICLR 2023 paper
quoted_support: In comprehensive ablation studies we show that the semantic entropy is more predictive of model accuracy on question answering data sets than comparable baselines.
